title: Uniform Linear-Time CNF Evaluator
statement: There exist a finite Boolean Turing machine $E$ and a natural number $A$ such that, for every CNF formula $\varphi$ over natural-number variable indices and every Boolean word $u$ for which each variable index in $\varphi$ is less than $|u|$, the machine $E$ computes the single-bit output $[\varphi(u)]$ on the paired encoding of the serialization of $\varphi$ and $u$, in exactly $A\bigl(|\langle\mathrm{enc}(\varphi),u\rangle|+1\bigr)$ steps. Here $\varphi(u)$ is the truth value under the assignment given by the bits of $u$, with variables beyond its length assigned false.
hypotheses_covered: existence of one finite Boolean machine $E$
arbitrary CNF formula over natural-number variable indices
every variable index in the formula is less than $|u|$
input is the pair encoding of the formula serialization and $u$
computation halts with the specified output and uses some space amount
replaced:
There exist a single finite machine $E$ and a constant $A$ such that for every CNF
formula $\varphi$ and every certificate word $u$ covering all variables of
$\varphi$ (each literal index below $|u|$), the machine $E$, run on the pair
encoding of the serialization of $\varphi$ with $u$, halts within
$A \cdot (\ell + 1)$ steps — $\ell$ the length of that paired input — and outputs
the single bit giving the truth value of $\varphi$ under the assignment read off
$u$.
